newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares dip early as demand stalls.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares dip early as demand stalls.

text.p: Singapore shares slipped early on Wednesday with demand sputtering to a halt on uncertainty over a recent technical recovery, dealers said.
"It hasn't been a very convincing follow-through. Investors can't decide because fundamentals are weak," a dealer with a local brokerage said, noting U.S. markets were in correction.
He said fund orders late on Tuesday, which pushed the index up sharply, were concentrated in selected core stocks and not lending support to the broader market.
At 0230 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 0.64 points at 2,003.62.
There was some demand for Malaysian over-the-counter issues, but dealers said demand was also relatively sluggish.
Top of the actives was SIA foreign, shored up by reports it was planning to buy a one third stake in Australia's Ansett.
The issue was unchanged at Singapore $12.30 on turnover of one million shares.
OUB foreign slipped five cents to S$8.75 after a spell of accumulation, as it was seen trading below its ex-rights price.
Creative Technology rose S$1.60 to S$25.70 in thin volume, catching up with rises overnight in New York, dealers said.
